legend: You have 2n%%ZSMJ0%% integers 1,2,…,2n%%ZSMJ1%%. You have to redistribute these 2n%%ZSMJ2%% elements into n%%ZSMJ3%% pairs. After that, you choose x%%ZSMJ4%% pairs and take minimum elements from them, and from the other n−x%%ZSMJ5%% pairs, you take maximum elements.
Your goal is to obtain the set of numbers {b1,b2,…,bn}%%ZSMJ6%% as the result of taking elements from the pairs.

What is the number of different x%%ZSMJ7%%-s (0≤x≤n%%ZSMJ8%%) such that it's possible to obtain the set b%%ZSMJ9%% if for each x%%ZSMJ10%% you can choose how to distribute numbers into pairs and from which x%%ZSMJ11%% pairs choose minimum elements?
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤t≤1000%%ZSMJ13%%) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains the integer n%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ15%%).
The second line of each test case contains n%%ZSMJ16%% integers b1,b2,…,bn%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤b1<b2<⋯<bn≤2n%%ZSMJ18%%) — the set you'd like to get.
It's guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ19%% over test cases doesn't exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ20%%.
output: For each test case, print one number — the number of different x%%ZSMJ21%%-s such that it's possible to obtain the set b%%ZSMJ22%%.
note: In the first test case, x=1%%ZSMJ23%% is the only option: you have one pair (1,2)%%ZSMJ24%% and choose the minimum from this pair.

In the second test case, there are three possible x%%ZSMJ25%%-s. If x=1%%ZSMJ26%%, then you can form the following pairs: (1,6)%%ZSMJ27%%, (2,4)%%ZSMJ28%%, (3,5)%%ZSMJ29%%, (7,9)%%ZSMJ30%%, (8,10)%%ZSMJ31%%. You can take minimum from (1,6)%%ZSMJ32%% (equal to 1%%ZSMJ33%%) and the maximum elements from all other pairs to get set b%%ZSMJ34%%.

If x=2%%ZSMJ35%%, you can form pairs (1,2)%%ZSMJ36%%, (3,4)%%ZSMJ37%%, (5,6)%%ZSMJ38%%, (7,9)%%ZSMJ39%%, (8,10)%%ZSMJ40%% and take the minimum elements from (1,2)%%ZSMJ41%%, (5,6)%%ZSMJ42%% and the maximum elements from the other pairs.

If x=3%%ZSMJ43%%, you can form pairs (1,3)%%ZSMJ44%%, (4,6)%%ZSMJ45%%, (5,7)%%ZSMJ46%%, (2,9)%%ZSMJ47%%, (8,10)%%ZSMJ48%% and take the minimum elements from (1,3)%%ZSMJ49%%, (4,6)%%ZSMJ50%%, (5,7)%%ZSMJ51%%.
In the third test case, x=0%%ZSMJ52%% is the only option: you can form pairs (1,3)%%ZSMJ53%%, (2,4)%%ZSMJ54%% and take the maximum elements from both of them.
